what: Failover drill (expert review stage D6): writes at 50 a second through a two-host connection string with target_session_attrs=read-write, the primary stopped without warning (pg_ctl stop -m immediate), the standby promoted 2 s later (a stand-in for Patroni's detection, ttl 30 s in production), an API instance listing both servers watched through /api/ready.
where: Development host, PostgreSQL 16, two clusters on one machine (ports 5436 and 5437), full Masslak schema; db/tools/failover_drill.py
reading: Both runs passed. Writing resumed 2.3 s after the first failed write, of which 2 s were the simulated detection; the API was not ready for 2.2 s and recovered on its own (its pool reconnected to the new primary). No acknowledged write was lost in either run; with a synchronous standby none can be. In production Patroni's detection adds up to about 30 s (ttl), which stays within the 60 s target; staging repeats the drill with Patroni and HAProxy (LAUNCH_GATES.md).
